title: ops huddle — controlplane routing auth quotas quick-swap
content:
TL;DR: Quick midweek ops huddle. Focus: (1) a small control plane rollback play for a routing edge case, (2) auth token expiry flapping in eu-west-3, (3) quota scheduler heuristic update trial. No P0s; two follow-ups and one on-call rotation ask.

Attendees: Jordan, Asha, Liam, Marisol, Chen, Elif (joined late).

Agenda:
- 10m: Recent incidents and current health signals
- 15m: Routing fallback experiment results + decide whether to roll forward
- 10m: Auth token expiry flapping (eu-west-3) — triage & mitigation
- 10m: Quotas: scheduler heuristic A/B trial start + metrics to watch
- 5m: Action items + owners

Notes / Observations:
1) Control plane health
- No active incidents. API latency 95th at 210ms for controlplane-api; spike observed on Oct 2 02:43 UTC (transient, 40s) correlated with a KV cache miss storm on cluster-7.
- KV cache TTLs: default 30s; suggested experiment: bump to 45s for routing prefix cache to reduce read amplification (see PLT-6342).
- Decision: schedule a non-disruptive canary to increase TTL on cluster-7 for 4-hour window next Wed 02:00-06:00 UTC. Owner: Asha.

2) Routing fallback experiment
- Summary: we ran the fallthrough weighting tweak (more aggressive primary->secondary fallback) for 12 hours behind a 10% traffic flag.
- Result: 8% reduction in tail latency for routing lookups but 3% increase in cross-region fallthroughs (more remote model invocations). Cost delta ~+1.1% token-cost at the test bucket.
- Tradeoff: improves user-visible latency at expense of cost and higher egress.
- Notes: observed one group of users (customer-team-spark) saw degraded relevance for rerank-type queries; hypothesize mismatch in model variant selection during fallback.
- Decision: pause rollout; create an A/B that restricts aggressive fallback to region-local customers only. Owner: Liam to open PLT-6411.

3) Auth token expiry flapping (eu-west-3)
- Symptom: short-lived spikes where token validation endpoint returned 401 for otherwise healthy requests. Happened ~03:00-04:20 UTC on Oct 3.
- Root cause hypothesis: clock skew on two auth-cache nodes (drift > 4s) causing premature rejection of JWTs using asymmetric tolerance.
- Fix applied: restarted affected auth-cache nodes and adjusted NTP poll interval; watchlist for 48h. Owner: Chen.
- Short mitigation: add temporary tolerance window (+5s) in validator for eu-west-3 only. Owner: Marisol to push hotfix config (feature-flagged). Rollback plan: revert flag if increases replay acceptance.

4) Quota scheduler heuristic trial
- New heuristic: schedule quota refill in larger batch for low-variance tenants to reduce scheduler churn. Experiment flagged at 15% of tenants for 72 hours starting Oct 4 00:00 UTC.
- Metrics to track: quota-pump CPU, refill-latency, per-tenant fairshare drift, and eviction-rate. Baseline eviction-rate = 0.32% (last 7d).
- Expected benefit: ~10% reduction in pump cycles, lower control-plane CPU, small improvement to tail latency during refill bursts.
- Owner: Elif (experiment config), Jordan (dashboard panels), Asha (rollback hooks).

Parking lot / open questions:
- Should we add a routing TTL heatmap to Console so teams can observe cache effectiveness per model? (Product ask).
- Do we want a live map of auth-cache node clock skew for on-call? (SRE tooling).
- How to instrument per-customer cost delta from routing fallbacks at a finer granularity?

Action items (owner, due):
- Asha: schedule TTL canary on cluster-7 and write runbook entries for TTL bump (due 2028-10-10).
- Liam: open PLT-6411 + draft constrained fallback A/B plan (due 2028-10-05).
- Chen: monitor auth-cache drift and report 48h status (due 2028-10-06).
- Marisol: push feature-flagged tolerance hotfix for eu-west-3 and coordinate with on-call (due 2028-10-04 18:00 UTC).
- Elif: deploy quota heuristic flag for 15% tenants and share dashboard links (due 2028-10-04 23:59 UTC).
- Jordan: create ad-hoc dashboard for quota pump CPU and eviction-rate (due 2028-10-05).

Blockers / Risks:
- If routing fallback increases egress for enterprise customers, sales may receive billing questions; we must have a rollback and customer-notify flow ready.
- Auth hotfix tolerance window could theoretically open a replay vector — mitigations: short timebox, monitor replay detector metrics, and immediate revert path.
- Quota heuristic may surface fairness regressions for noisy tenants; set early kill thresholds.

Follow-ups / syncs planned:
- Deep-dive with SRE next Tue 2028-10-09 to review auth drift telemetry and discuss automated alerting.
- Routing fallthrough A/B review mid-experiment (after 24 hours of traffic) — Liam to schedule.

Meeting notes: quick conversational fragments below (keepsakes):
- "We saw the mesh go egress-happy when fallback hit remote rack — surprising but reproducible with synthetic."
- "TTL bump is low-risk, but let's be explicit about cache invalidation costs — document in runbook."
- "Auth clock skew again… seriously, need better on-call tooling for time sync."

Appendix: useful links and snippets:
- PLT-6342 (cache-ttl-canary) — summary: small canary config, rollback script included.
- PLT-6411 (routing-fallback-ab) — draft ticket (Liam) to scope cost guardrails.
- GH #9123 — quota scheduler proto PR (benchmarks included).

End notes: keep huddle cadence at twice-weekly while experiments are running; reduces cognitive load for on-call and gives time to observe. Next quick-swap huddle: Fri 2028-10-06 09:00 UTC.

Scratchpad / quick TODOs for myself:
- add a watch alert: auth-validator-401-rate > 0.05% sustained for 5m -> page oncall.
- write short blurb for product about routing cost vs latency tradeoff for next Sync.
- validate NTP config across all eu-west-3 hosts and add a heartbeat metric.
